title: Career Roadmap: Communications Executive
summary: A Communications Executive develops and delivers communication that helps an organisation share information, maintain its reputation and engage effectively with employees, customers, media and other stakeholders.

facts.Current degree: Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies – Media, Communication & Culture

about.label: Primary Industries
about.text: Corporate Communications, Public Relations, Media, Technology, Education, Healthcare, Nonprofits

about.label: Suitable For
about.text: Students interested in writing, storytelling, public relations, branding, media, content strategy and stakeholder engagement

blocks.text: A Communications Executive develops and delivers communication that helps an organisation share information, maintain its reputation and engage effectively with employees, customers, media and other stakeholders.

Students specialising in Media, Communication & Culture develop relevant skills in writing, cultural analysis, storytelling, audience understanding and media literacy. These skills can be applied to corporate communication, public relations, internal communication and digital content.
Key responsibilities

items.text: Draft press releases, announcements, newsletters and corporate updates.
Prepare social media posts, website content and communication materials.
Support public relations campaigns and media outreach.
Coordinate internal communication with employees and leadership teams.
Maintain brand tone, messaging consistency and communication calendars.
Monitor media coverage and public responses.
Organise communication activities, events and stakeholder interactions.
Assist with crisis communication, reputation management and reporting.

blocks.label: Example
blocks.text: A technology company launches a new product. The Communications Executive prepares the announcement, coordinates media materials, supports social media communication and tracks audience responses.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: The exact scope varies by employer. A Communications Executive in corporate communications may focus on internal messaging and reputation, while one in a PR agency may focus more on media relations, campaigns and client coordination.
Undergraduate route
Liberal Arts – Media, Communication & Culture
Develop a foundation in communication theory, media studies, cultural analysis, storytelling and audience behaviour.
Professional communication skills
Learn business writing, editing, presentation, public relations, brand communication and digital content development.
Practical experience
Build a portfolio through student publications, event communication, social media campaigns, internships and communication projects.
Further study options
Depending on career goals and admission eligibility, consider:

items.text: MA Communication or Mass Communication
MA Public Relations and Corporate Communication
Postgraduate programmes in Strategic Communication
MA Digital Media or Media Management
MBA in Marketing or Communications-oriented management
Specialised courses in crisis communication, brand communication or public affairs

blocks.text: A postgraduate degree is not mandatory for many entry-level communication positions. Strong writing, a practical portfolio, internships and stakeholder-management skills can be sufficient for numerous opportunities.
Year 1 — Communication Foundations

items.text: Study communication theory, media literacy and audience behaviour.
Improve grammar, writing, editing and presentation skills.
Read professional news, corporate announcements and press releases.
Learn the basics of storytelling, visual communication and digital media.

blocks.label: Mini-project
blocks.text: Create a communication pack for a fictional student event, including an announcement, newsletter and social media posts.
Year 2 — Content and Public Relations

items.text: Practise writing press releases, media pitches and corporate emails.
Learn content planning, editorial calendars and brand voice.
Explore public relations, media monitoring and reputation management.
Develop basic graphic-design and content-publishing skills.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Plan a two-week communication campaign for a campus initiative or student organisation.
Year 3 — Strategy and Measurement

items.text: Learn audience segmentation and communication planning.
Practise stakeholder mapping and message development.
Understand engagement metrics, media coverage and campaign reporting.
Explore internal communication and crisis-response principles.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Create an integrated campaign with defined objectives, audience segments, messaging, channels and evaluation metrics.
Final Year — Industry Readiness

items.text: Complete an internship in corporate communications, PR, media or digital content.
Prepare a portfolio containing press releases, campaigns, newsletters and reports.
Practise professional presentations, client communication and deadline management.
Apply for Communications Executive, PR Executive and Corporate Communications Intern roles.
Prepare for writing tests, editing exercises and campaign-planning interviews.

blocks.text: Corporate Communications Executive
Communicates company news, leadership messages, organisational updates and brand information.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: corporate writing, stakeholder communication and message consistency.
Public Relations Executive
Supports media relations, press releases, public announcements and reputation-building activities.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: media outreach, news judgment, relationship-building and media monitoring.
Internal Communications Executive
Helps employees understand organisational changes, leadership decisions, company policies and workplace initiatives.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: employee newsletters, internal announcements and change communication.
Digital Communications Executive
Manages digital messaging across websites, email campaigns, social platforms and online communication channels.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: digital writing, content calendars, publishing and performance metrics.
Crisis and Reputation Communications
Supports communication during sensitive events, service disruptions, public criticism or organisational changes.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: factual messaging, coordination, approvals and rapid response.
A strong portfolio should demonstrate the ability to adapt messages to different audiences, write accurately and coordinate communication across channels.

blocks.text: Potential employers include PR agencies, corporate communications departments, media companies, technology firms, educational institutions, healthcare organisations, nonprofits and consulting firms.
For each portfolio project, include the objective, target audience, key message, communication channels, sample content and evaluation method. Clearly identify fictional campaigns as simulations.

rows.text: Media-monitoring platforms and organised coverage trackers
Slack, Microsoft Teams or equivalent tools

blocks.text: Tool choice depends on the employer. Strong writing and sound communication judgement remain more important than familiarity with a long list of platforms.

blocks.text: Prioritise courses that include writing assignments, campaign exercises and feedback. Certificates can support preparation but do not replace practical experience or a strong portfolio.

Progression depends on communication quality, industry knowledge, stakeholder relationships, campaign outcomes and leadership ability.

blocks.text: AI can assist with drafting and summarisation, but all public-facing communication should be checked for accuracy, confidentiality, tone and consistency with approved organisational messaging.

Final Recommendation

For students pursuing Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies with a Media, Communication & Culture specialisation, Communications Executive is a practical career pathway combining writing, audience understanding, public relations and organisational communication.

Prioritise professional writing, editing, PR fundamentals, stakeholder management and digital communication. Build a portfolio with realistic communication materials and complete relevant internships to demonstrate that you can turn an organisation's objectives into accurate, clear and audience-appropriate messages.
